transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I'm a barber. I actually graduated a couple years ago. Barber school was intense, honestly, way more hours than people think. We had this one instructor, Mr. Henderson, who used to make us sweep the floors for hours if we left a single clipper out. Strict guy, but he knew his stuff. 

Anyway, working at the shop now... I'm here because I’ve gotten to where I’ll do almost anything to avoid using the straight razor at work. It's getting ridiculous. I'll switch clients with my coworker, or I'll tell the customer the blade’s missing, or I'll literally just hide it in my drawer. My coworker Dave actually owes me like fifty bucks from a fantasy football league we did last season, so he doesn't mind taking my clients when I ask. But yeah, if I can’t get out of it and I actually have to do the shave... I’m just shaking through the whole thing.
Is the anxiety you’re feeling mostly related to using the straight razor, or have you noticed it happening in other parts of your life too?

Honestly, it’s really just the razor. Like, I know it’s just a tool I trained with, right? I can use clippers all day long. Actually, I just bought this new pair of cordless Wahl clippers, the gold edition ones? Man, they run so smooth, and they hold a charge for like three days straight. My buddy at the shop was trying to buy them off me yesterday because they’re sold out everywhere online right now. I told him no way, obviously, it took me a month on a waitlist to get them. 

But yeah, clippers are totally fine. Scissors, fine. But when that straight razor is just sitting open at my station... I don't know, it just feels like I’m about to hurt somebody, or like I'm gonna slip and cut myself really badly. Which makes no sense because I passed my practical exam with flying colors. The state examiner even complimented my fade, which they never do. So yeah, I don't really get anxious about anything else, just the razor.
Have you ever felt anxious or avoided situations where you felt you were being closely watched or judged, like speaking in public or performing tasks in front of others?

No, not really. I mean, people watch me cut hair all day long, you know? The shop is set up so everyone can see everyone else's station, and we have these massive floor-to-ceiling windows facing out onto the street. Actually, the owner, Marcus, he just had them professionally washed on Tuesday by this guy who used to come in for haircuts. He started his own power-washing business recently, bought a whole van, got custom decals made, the works. Good for him, honestly. Though he uses this weird squeegee technique that always leaves streaks right at the bottom left corner of my window... I didn't have the heart to tell him, since he gave us a discount. 

But yeah, wait, what were you asking? Oh, being judged or speaking in public. Nah, that stuff is totally fine. I gave a best man speech for my brother last year in front of like two hundred people and I didn't sweat it at all. It's really just the razor that messes with me.
When you’re around the straight razor and start feeling anxious, do you notice any physical symptoms like sweating, shaking, or a racing heart?

Yeah, definitely. It's like, the second I hear a client ask for a razor shave, or even if I just see the blade flipped open on the counter, my chest gets super tight. My hands get all sweaty, and it’s like my body just wants to back away before my brain even catches up. 

Speaking of backing away, I actually had to back my car into a spot this morning because the parking lot next door was totally jammed. There’s this new bakery that opened up down the block, right next to the dry cleaners. They do these crazy cronut things, like half croissant, half donut? My girlfriend is obsessed with them. She made me wait in line for forty-five minutes on Sunday just to get the pistachio cream ones. Forty-five minutes! And honestly, they weren't even that good, way too sweet for me. I’m more of a savory guy, you know? Like a good everything bagel with scallion cream cheese. There used to be this spot near my barber school that did the best bagels... 

But yeah, my heart definitely races and my hands shake really bad when I have to hold that razor. It's wild how fast it happens.
Have you ever felt this kind of anxiety or avoidance with other tools or situations where there's a chance of causing harm, like driving or handling something delicate?

No, driving is totally fine. I actually really like driving. I just put these new all-weather Michelin tires on my Civic on Tuesday. The guy at the tire shop tried to upsell me on this premium alignment package, which is such a scam, right? Like, my uncle used to be a mechanic down in Florida, and he always told me they just hook it up to the computer and barely adjust anything unless you've hit a massive pothole or been in a wreck. 

My uncle actually just retired last month and bought this huge RV. He's driving it across the country right now with his golden retriever, Buster. He keeps sending me pictures of random diners he stops at. He sent me one yesterday of a waffle that was literally the size of a steering wheel, just completely covered in strawberry syrup. Looked amazing, honestly, though I don't know how he eats like that and sits in a driver's seat all day... 

Wait, sorry, what did you ask me? Oh, right, driving or other tools. Nah, I don't get that weird panic feeling with anything else. Scissors, driving, handling delicate stuff, it's all good. I never worry about causing harm with anything else. It's really just the straight razor.
Has this kind of intense anxiety or avoidance ever happened with any other specific tools or objects, even if they weren't related to your job?

No, not really. I mean, I'm pretty handy around the house. I actually just put together this huge IKEA dresser for my bedroom last weekend. It was the Hemnes one, you know? The one with the eight drawers. Man, the instructions for that thing were basically written in hieroglyphics. I swear I spent like three hours just trying to figure out which screws went where, and I still ended up with two extra pieces of wood at the end. I just shoved them in the back of my closet and hoped for the best. 

My girlfriend was supposed to help me, but she got totally distracted watching this true crime documentary on Netflix. It was about this guy who scammed all these people out of millions of dollars by pretending to be a European prince or something. Crazy how people fall for that stuff, right? Like, if some guy messages you on Instagram saying he needs a hundred grand to fix his private jet, maybe do a background check first. 

But yeah, anyway... what were we talking about? Oh, other tools or objects. No, I don't get that weird panic feeling with anything else. Hammers, drills, whatever. It's literally just the straight razor that gets me.
Can you think of any other specific situations—like using different tools, handling sharp objects, or performing tasks under pressure—where you've felt the same level of anxiety or urge to avoid it?

No, nothing else. Like I said, I use clippers, shears, trimmers all day long, totally fine. I actually just bought a new pair of Japanese steel shears online. They were ridiculously expensive, but they cut like absolute butter. I had to wait three weeks for them to ship because they got stuck in customs or something. 

Speaking of shipping, my mail carrier is the worst. He keeps leaving my packages on the bottom step instead of bringing them up to the porch, and it rained on Tuesday and soaked this box of vintage comic books I bought off eBay. I collect Spider-Man comics, specifically the Todd McFarlane run from the 90s. The artwork is just incredible, way better than the stuff they put out now. I tried calling the post office to complain, but you just get put on hold for an hour listening to that awful elevator music. 

But um, yeah, what was the question? Other situations? No, it's just the straight razor. I can handle anything else under pressure, no problem. It's just that one specific blade.
Do you have any fear or avoidance of other sharp objects, like knives or scalpels, even outside of work?

No, not at all. I cook a lot at home, actually. I just bought this beautiful set of German knives, Wüsthof, you know? They are so sharp, you could probably slice a tomato mid-air with them. I made this incredible beef bourguignon last night. Took me like four hours. You have to braise the meat low and slow, and I used this really nice Pinot Noir I found at Trader Joe's. 

It's funny, the cashier at Trader Joe's was telling me about how she's trying to get into nursing school, but the waitlists are insane right now. She said she's been waiting for like two years just to get a spot. I can't imagine waiting that long for something. I'm way too impatient. Like when I go to a restaurant, if I have to wait more than twenty minutes for a table, I'm out. There's this taco place down the street from my apartment that always has a line wrapped around the block. I don't care how good the al pastor is, I'm not standing on the sidewalk for an hour. 

Wait, sorry, what did you ask me about? Oh, knives. Yeah, no, knives are totally fine. I chop vegetables, carve meat, whatever. It doesn't bother me at all. It's literally just the straight razor.
